method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading and reverse paraphrase; not independent or human review.
scope: All seventeen translated content blocks on non-enumerability by reduction, reduction direction and six exercises.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: To reduce enumerating B to enumerating A, give a surjection A→B so an enumeration x1,x2,… of A yields f(x1),f(x2),… enumerating B.
samples.checks: The direction, domain/codomain, surjectivity requirement and induced list are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Map each subset Z of positive integers to its binary characteristic sequence, with value 1 exactly at positions belonging to Z.
samples.checks: The membership biconditional, example sequences and surjectivity proof are exact; OLSIZ-006 marks the source's undefined s_k subscript.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Surjectivity converts a hypothetical enumeration of Pow(PosInt) into one of Bin^omega, contradicting the preceding non-enumerability theorem.
samples.checks: All theorem references, list values, hypotheses and contradiction direction remain unchanged.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A surjection from Bin^omega onto a finite set does not make the finite target nonenumerable, and a non-surjective map from an enumerable domain cannot transfer an enumeration of the whole target.
samples.checks: The first-bit map and failed-surjectivity warning are preserved; OLSIZ-007 identifies the malformed finite-string example.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Exercises apply reduction to sets of integer pairs, Nat-valued functions, infinite Nat sequences, partial zero-valued functions, surjective binary-valued functions and the reals.
samples.checks: Each function space, total/partial distinction, surjectivity condition and target conclusion remains exact.

limitations: T074 is provisional direction-explicit vocabulary open to correction.
No independent linguistic certification has been performed.
